Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.

=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

## Buyer’s overall position

**The Seller’s package should not be accepted as drafted.** It combines unresolved completion risks with broad provisions that could prevent Wattlebridge recovering for those same risks. Disclosure of a problem is not a substitute for fixing it, allocating its cost or providing an effective indemnity.

This review is based on the supplied update and Disclosure Letter—not the full SPA or underlying DD documents. The disclosures identify issues requiring verification; they do not establish every underlying legal or factual conclusion.

## 1. Resolve the key completion and price risks

### Bluefen consent — a substantive completion condition

Bluefen represents approximately **AUD 3.6 million, or 30% of FY26 revenue**. No final consent or evidence of satisfaction of its associated conditions has been supplied.

**Push back:**
- Require effective written change-of-control consent **and satisfaction of all associated conditions** before Completion.
- Consent must not introduce materially adverse amendments, charges, termination rights or other unacceptable conditions.
- Delivery of a consent document alone must not deem the condition satisfied.
- Require the Seller to pursue consent actively, report progress and obtain Buyer approval before agreeing concessions.
- Preserve a Buyer-only waiver right and a termination right if the condition is not satisfied by the agreed long-stop date.

**Why:** Reasonable endeavours are a process obligation, not assurance that a major revenue contract will survive on acceptable terms.

### Riverlark facility — discharge at Completion, not afterwards

Approximately **AUD 3.2 million remains outstanding**, and no final security discharge is included.

**Push back:**
- Obtain a current payout statement, including interest, fees and break costs.
- Provide for repayment directly from Seller proceeds through the completion funds flow, consistently with the debt-free/cash-free price mechanics.
- Require effective releases of relevant security, guarantees and other obligations at Completion, supported by binding lender undertakings and an agreed registration process.
- Address any change-of-control default or lender consent needed before discharge.

**Why:** A promise to provide a release after Completion leaves the Buyer owning a company exposed to lender enforcement. Administrative registration may follow under controlled arrangements; the substantive discharge protection should not.

### Completion bonuses — expressly allocate the entire cost

The **AUD 420,000** bonuses are triggered by Completion and continued employment, but are omitted from the draft funds flow.

**Push back:**
- Verify the entitlement, payment timing and continued-employment conditions.
- Expressly allocate the agreed Seller-borne amount through a debt-like adjustment, transaction-expense deduction or payment from Seller proceeds.
- Determine applicable superannuation, payroll tax and other on-costs and allocate those too.
- Ensure the treatment works even if payment becomes due after Completion, with protection for amounts omitted or understated.

**Why:** Calling these “a matter for the Seller” does not prevent the Company—and economically the Buyer—from bearing them. Avoid double counting through both working capital and another adjustment.

### Sandbar renewals — investigate before accepting “ordinary course”

Three related renewals total **AUD 330,000**. The disclosures do not establish their timing, necessity, termination rights or accounting treatment.

**Push back:**
- Review the documents together, including service periods, cancellation rights, accrued liabilities and any unusual commitments.
- Apply interim operating covenants to the **aggregate related commitment**, preventing consent thresholds being avoided through separate contracts.
- Allocate costs under the agreed working-capital, debt-like and transaction-expense definitions.

**Why:** These are not automatically Seller debt or improper expenditure. They may be genuine future operating costs, but the Seller has not substantiated that conclusion.

## 2. Obtain effective protection for identified risks

### Ironquay IP — secure ownership, not merely payment protection

Transfer of SOW3 Project Materials depends on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. The records show **AUD 180,000 open**, but do not independently prove non-payment. Neither a receipt nor confirmatory assignment is available.

**Push back:**
- Reconcile the full SOW3 balance and obtain evidence of cleared payment.
- Obtain a confirmatory assignment or other satisfactory evidence that all relevant rights have vested, including appropriate contributor rights.
- Make resolution a completion requirement if the materials are material to the business.
- Expand the indemnity beyond the identified payment to losses arising from the relevant pre-Completion title defect or dispute, including justified defence, remediation and replacement costs.

**Why:** An indemnity limited to a fee does not compensate for losing essential IP or the ability to use it. Any special indemnity must expressly survive disclosure and knowledge provisions and avoid unintended general limitations.

### Export/privacy incident — investigate without assuming a confirmed breach

The material records an unintended external delivery and potentially **1,240 records**, but does not establish access, final scope, notification obligations or loss.

**Push back:**
- Require prompt investigation, evidence preservation, containment and a documented assessment of contractual and applicable privacy/data-breach obligations.
- Obtain updates through Completion, including whether access occurred and whether the export was secured, revoked or deleted.
- Require legally necessary notifications within applicable deadlines; Buyer consultation must not delay compliance.
- Seek a specific indemnity for the pre-Completion incident and related failures, covering appropriate investigation, remediation and third-party liabilities, with fines covered only to the extent lawful.
- Consider a targeted completion condition, escrow or retention if material exposure remains unresolved.

**Why:** “Preliminary” does not mean immaterial. Equally, the current evidence does **not** justify asserting a confirmed notifiable breach or a quantified liability.

## 3. Rebalance the liability regime

### General cap, thresholds and survival

The proposed **20% cap (AUD 4.8 million)**, **AUD 25,000 de minimis**, **AUD 250,000 deductible basket** and **18-month period** operate cumulatively to restrict recovery.

**Buyer position:**
- Negotiate a higher general cap, informed by diligence, available insurance and Seller creditworthiness.
- Reduce the thresholds and seek a **tipping basket**, so qualifying losses are recoverable from the first dollar once the basket is exceeded.
- Aggregate related claims when applying the de minimis.
- Seek a longer general warranty period—**24 months is a reasonable opening position**, allowing two reporting cycles.
- Preserve timely notified claims until resolution; reject onerous notification particulars or short mandatory proceedings deadlines.

These figures are negotiating positions, not mandatory legal standards. The eventual compromise should be assessed as a package.

### Fundamental/title, tax and IP must not simply inherit the general regime

**Reject administrative simplicity as the justification for limiting title and capacity protection to 20% and 18 months.**

Seek:
- **Title/capacity:** separate protection up to at least the full purchase price, with an appropriately longer survival period.
- **Tax:** a dedicated covenant/indemnity for agreed pre-Completion tax exposures, with tailored exclusions, conduct provisions and survival aligned with relevant assessment and recovery periods.
- **IP:** meaningful ownership, licensing and infringement warranties, with separately negotiated protection where warranted; the known Ironquay issue needs specific treatment.
- **Specific indemnities:** express, risk-specific caps, periods and procedures rather than accidental application of the general regime.

Also ensure warranty limitations do not inadvertently restrict completion payments, price adjustments, debt discharge obligations or other distinct contractual obligations.

### “All Claims” limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance

Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 potentially undermine every protection negotiated elsewhere.

**Push back:**
- Replace blanket application with an express allocation of limitations by claim type.
- Preserve claims for fraud and fraudulent misrepresentation, and rights that cannot lawfully be excluded.
- Preserve enforcement of payment obligations, agreed indemnities and appropriate equitable relief.
- Ensure non-reliance language does not negate express warranties or representations incorporated into the agreement.
- Check loss definitions and exclusions do not eliminate foreseeable business interruption, remediation or third-party liabilities central to the identified risks.

Under Australian law, exclusion and non-reliance clauses do not automatically eliminate statutory misleading-conduct exposure, although they can affect reliance and causation. **Do not rely on later litigation to repair defective drafting.**

## 4. Reject blanket disclosure and constructive Buyer knowledge

The combination of general data-room/public-register disclosure and clause 8.3 could defeat claims for matters nobody actually identified.

**Push back:**
- Require disclosures to be sufficiently specific and detailed to identify the nature and scope of the exception to the relevant warranty.
- Reject blanket disclosure of everything “contained or referred to” in the data room and unrestricted public records.
- Fix and retain an agreed indexed data-room snapshot; agree the treatment of later disclosures.
- Delete “discoverable” knowledge and automatic attribution of advisers’ knowledge.
- Prefer no knowledge exclusion; if conceded, confine it to actual knowledge of named Buyer personnel of clearly identified facts, without a duty of inquiry.
- Expressly preserve specific indemnities and completion obligations notwithstanding disclosure or knowledge.

**Why:** Disclosure ordinarily qualifies warranties; it should not silently transfer known liabilities or excuse agreed remedial steps. The Seller’s reservation that it admits nothing neither resolves those liabilities nor proves its negotiating position.

## 5. Complete targeted verification—without inventing consent requirements

- **Share title:** DD-012 is evidence, not complete verification. Reconcile the register with corporate records, share issues/transfers, beneficial ownership, encumbrances, options and other rights. Require transfer of 100% of issued shares free of encumbrances and appropriate completion deliverables.
- **Office lease:** verify and comply with the notification obligation. The supplied material does **not** establish a landlord consent requirement.
- **Mossvale:** an assignment restriction does **not**, without more, establish that a share sale requires consent. Review the complete contract for separate change-of-control provisions.
- **Disclosure currency:** the disclosure snapshot is 22 September 2026. Require refreshed diligence and bring-down information through signing and Completion, without automatic qualification of warranties by new disclosures.

## Recommended negotiating priorities

1. **Completion gates:** effective Bluefen consent and conditions; Riverlark repayment and release; satisfactory resolution of material Ironquay ownership issues.
2. **Protect the economics:** expressly allocate bonuses and on-costs, reconcile debt and funds flow, and investigate Sandbar commitments.
3. **Contain identified exposure:** complete the incident investigation and negotiate targeted indemnities, backed by escrow or retention where justified.
4. **Repair enforceability:** remove blanket “all Claims” restrictions, constructive knowledge and general disclosure; separate title, tax and specific-risk protection.
5. **Verify recovery:** assess Seller covenant strength and obtain security for material deferred liabilities. A strong indemnity is of limited value if the Seller cannot pay.
